favourite.heading: Why Tulsa can pull away
bullets: Tulsa is the better football team by 18.5 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 86% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+18.5 pts).
Playing at Tulsa is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).

underdog.heading: Why East Texas A&M can keep it close
bullets: The outcome range is 15.5 points wide at one sigma — p10 -1.4 to p90 +43.6 for Tulsa, so a projection of +22.6 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 6%.
70% of the model’s own input contract was empty for this game — no starter, injury, schedule or per-player talent context reached it, so the number leans on team strength more than it should.
East Texas A&M is not in the FBS rating set, so EdgeDesk cannot measure what it does well. An unmeasured opponent is an unknown, not a weak one, and the size of the gap is not established.
